$comment: The lowest id each product type may mint, per environment. Keyed '<family>:<series>'.
Counters (data/counters.json) and run history (data/runs/) live on one machine and are not in
git, so a fresh clone used to start every series at its template's sampleStart — an id that
was loaded long ago. A sandbox refresh empties Salesforce but not IDMS, so the collision check
sees those ids as free and IDMS rejects the load with 'already exists'.
This file is the shared memory of what IDMS holds. The allocator never starts below it, nor
below the local counter, nor at or below the highest id this machine minted, nor at or below
the highest id the org already holds in the series' band. Raise a value and commit it when a
series moves to a new range (as testing DHUB did on 2026-11-20, to 4011600001, after another
loader's IDMS-only hubs rejected two batches). Values only ever go up.
Seeded 2026-11-24 from the counters on the machine that had been doing the loads.
